title: 15 以前隔着屏幕16 悸动与多单纯
content_zh:
翌日，下午。
周娘子来找他，一见面，就发现曹笔看她的眼神有点躲闪，当即好奇道：“恩公，您怎么了？是不是有什么事？需要妾身帮忙吗？”
“咳咳~没事儿，可能是昨晚没睡好。”
曹笔随便找了个借口，不好意思看对方的眼睛，怕被对方察觉。
“真的？”
周娘子发现了他的异常，视线追着他的视线跑。
曹笔点了点头，赶紧转移话题。
“嗯，对了，你来找我，可是有事？”
此问一出，周娘子的脸色略显严肃，犹豫了一下道：“恩公……”
曹笔见她有些纠结，当即道：“无需顾忌，有什么事，直说吧。”
周娘子闻言，看着他的眼睛，征询道：“恩公，您能不能陪妾身去个地方？”
“能！”
“恩公，您不问去哪里？有没有危险？”
“我现在是你的近身侍卫，我只需要负责保护你，其它的，不该我过问。”
周娘子沉默了一息，沉声解释道：“城外三十里，有个村子。
有人给妾身来信，说知道妾身夫君死亡的真相。
约妾身今日酉时，在那个村子见面。”
“在此之前，妾身查了大半年，什么都没查到。
朝廷公告说，夫君是擅自行动，中了凶骨人埋伏，死了。
可妾身不信，他不是那样冒进的人。”

她顿了顿，声音低了些。
“这半年来，妾身派人暗中调查，可每次查到一点线索，就断了。
像是有人故意在掩盖什么，原本妾身都快放弃了，以为是自己多想了。”
“可前不久，突然有人送来一封信，说知道真相，妾身……”
曹笔闻言，知道她在担心什么，也猜到了她想做什么，当即打断了她：“不必多说，是真是假，去一看便知。”
……
马车出了城，往西北方向走。
天色渐暗，路越来越窄，两边的林子越来越密。
曹笔骑马跟在马车旁边，手按在刀柄上。
他的目光没有看向前方，而是若有若无地扫过身后的方向。
有人在跟着。
从出城开始，就有三个人，一直保持着距离，藏在官道两侧的林子里。
普通人察觉不到，但他能。
那三个人跟了五六里，忽然停了。
然后，天上多了一只前世没见过的鸟。
盘旋在高空，一直跟着马车。
曹笔抬头看了一眼。
那鸟飞得很高，普通人只会当成寻常的飞禽。
但他感知到，那鸟的眼睛，一直在盯着下面的马车。
他收回目光，脸上什么表情都没有。
content_en:
The next day, afternoon.
Mrs. Zhou came to see him. When they met, she found that Cao Bi looked at her a little evasively. She immediately asked curiously: "My dear friend, what's wrong with you? Is there something wrong? Do you need my help?"
"Ahem~ It's okay, maybe I didn't sleep well last night."
Cao Bi made a random excuse and was embarrassed to look into the other person's eyes for fear of being noticed by the other party.
"Really?"
Madam Zhou noticed something unusual about him and her eyes followed his.
Cao Bi nodded and quickly changed the topic.
"Well, by the way, you came to see me, but something happened?"
As soon as this question came out, Mrs. Zhou's face turned slightly serious, she hesitated and said: "My benefactor..."
Seeing that she was a little confused, Cao Bi immediately said: "No need to worry, if you have anything to do, just tell me."
After hearing this, Mrs. Zhou looked into his eyes and asked, "My lord, can you accompany me to a place?"
"Yes!"
"My dear friend, don't you ask where you are going? Is there any danger?"
"I am your personal bodyguard now. I only need to be responsible for protecting you, and I am not responsible for the rest."
Madam Zhou was silent for a moment and explained in a deep voice: "There is a village thirty miles outside the city.
Someone wrote to me, saying that he knew the truth about the death of my husband.
I have arranged to meet you in that village at You time today. "
"Before this, I searched for more than half a year and found nothing.
The court announced that the husband acted on his own initiative and was ambushed by a ruthless man and died.
But I don’t believe it, he is not that kind of person. "
She paused and her voice became lower.
"In the past six months, I have sent people to investigate secretly, but every time I found some clues, they were discontinued.
It seemed like someone was deliberately covering up something. I almost gave up, thinking that I was overthinking it. "
"But not long ago, someone suddenly sent a letter saying that he knew the truth, I..."
Upon hearing this, Cao Bi knew what she was worried about and guessed what she wanted to do, so he immediately interrupted her: "No need to say more, you will know if it is true or false, just go and take a look."
…
The carriage left the city and headed northwest.
The sky is getting darker, the road is getting narrower and narrower, and the woods on both sides are getting denser and denser.
Cao Bi rode next to the carriage, his hand on the handle of the knife.
His eyes did not look forward, but glanced in the direction behind him.
Someone is following.
From the moment they left the city, there were three people who kept their distance and hid in the woods on both sides of the official road.
Ordinary people can't notice it, but he can.
The three men followed for five or six miles and suddenly stopped.
Then, there was a bird in the sky that I had never seen before.
Hovering high in the sky, following the carriage.
Cao Bi looked up.
The bird flew so high that ordinary people would just regard it as an ordinary bird.
But he sensed that the bird's eyes had been staring at the carriage below.
He looked away, with no expression on his face.
